lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The king had a dream that terrified him. He demanded his wise men tell him not just what it meant — but what it was.

lines.speaker: nebuchadnezzar
lines.text: Interpret my dream — or ALL the wise men of Babylon die. Including you, Daniel.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No human could answer. But Daniel didn't guess. He prayed first.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: There is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Your dream: a statue of terrifying brightness. Gold head. Silver chest. Bronze belly. Iron legs. Feet of clay.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: You are the gold head, O King. But after you will come other kingdoms — and in the end, God's kingdom will crush them all and stand forever.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The king could have been angry at the news. Instead, he did something no one expected.

choices.label: Daniel softens the message 😬
choices.note: A flattering reading protects favor with the king now — but dents Discernment.

choices.label: Daniel delivers it plainly ✅
choices.note: The true reading, even the uncomfortable parts. That's what earns the king's respect.

lines.speaker: nebuchadnezzar
lines.text: Your God is the God of gods and Lord of kings — a revealer of mysteries!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel used his promotion not to protect himself, but to save the other wise men who had no power to answer.
